skill.name: timescaledb
skill.description: TimescaleDB guidance for PostgreSQL time-series development, including hypertables, continuous aggregates, compression, time buckets, and installation references.
skill.summary: Build and tune TimescaleDB time-series applications with bundled PostgreSQL reference material.
skill.author: 2025Emma

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by generated Markdown, SQL examples, and TimescaleDB documentation text. I confirmed user-visible privileged installation patterns, a curl-to-bash installer, and two oversized reference files that were not statically scanned. I also found a destructive DROP EXTENSION quick-reference example; no prompt injection evidence was found.

remediation.issue: Privileged installation commands appear in reference content.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear warnings and require explicit user confirmation before suggesting sudo, dnf, apt, systemctl, or package source commands.

remediation.issue: A curl-to-bash installer command is included.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer package-manager instructions with source verification, checksums, or signed release guidance instead of direct remote script execution.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md includes a destructive DROP EXTENSION example without warning.
remediation.suggestion: Remove it from the quick reference or label it as a destructive recovery operation with backup and rollback prerequisites.

remediation.issue: Two reference files were too large for static scanning.
remediation.suggestion: Split oversized reference files into smaller topical files so automated and manual review can cover all content reliably.

content.value_statement: Time-series data work needs correct schema, retention, and aggregation choices. This skill gives TimescaleDB reference guidance for PostgreSQL developers and database teams.
actual_capabilities: Explains hypertables and time partitioning for PostgreSQL time-series data.
Guides continuous aggregates, refresh policies, and real-time aggregate behavior.
Provides compression and hypercore guidance for storage and query performance.
Helps write TimescaleDB SQL for time buckets, retention, and analytics.
Summarizes installation, Rails integration, Docker, Kubernetes, and package setup references.
Points users to API, performance, and tutorial sections in bundled references.
limitations: Does not connect to databases or execute SQL by itself.
Contains generated documentation snapshots, which may lag current TimescaleDB releases.
Some examples include privileged shell commands that need human review before use.
Large reference files may be hard to audit manually.

use_cases.title: Design Time-Series Schemas
use_cases.description: Choose hypertable dimensions, indexes, and chunk intervals for event, metric, or sensor workloads.

use_cases.title: Improve Analytics Performance
use_cases.description: Plan continuous aggregates, compression policies, and time bucket queries for faster dashboards.

use_cases.title: Operate TimescaleDB Deployments
use_cases.description: Review installation, configuration, migration, and maintenance guidance before changing environments.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Hypertable
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how a TimescaleDB hypertable works for a simple sensor readings table. Include when to use time and space dimensions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a TimescaleDB schema for application events with tenant IDs, timestamps, and retention requirements. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Aggregates
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my continuous aggregate plan for hourly metrics. Suggest refresh windows, indexes, compression choices, and risks to test.

prompt_templates.title: Review Installation Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a cautious TimescaleDB installation checklist for Ubuntu. Separate commands that require elevated privileges from verification steps.

output_examples.input: I need to store sensor readings every second for several devices.
output_examples.output: A schema plan with a hypertable, recommended partition dimensions, index guidance, and retention considerations.

output_examples.input: My dashboard query over daily metrics is slow.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting path covering time buckets, continuous aggregates, refresh policy timing, and compression effects.

output_examples.input: I want to install TimescaleDB on a Linux server.
output_examples.output: A staged checklist that highlights privileged commands, package source changes, and post-install verification.

best_practices: Confirm TimescaleDB version and PostgreSQL version before applying reference commands.
Test schema, compression, and retention changes on staging data before production use.
Review every privileged shell command before running it on a workstation or server.
anti_patterns: Do not paste generated installation commands into production without checking package sources.
Do not use continuous aggregates without validating refresh windows and late-arriving data behavior.
Do not drop extensions, chunks, or policies unless you have a rollback plan.

faq.question: Does this skill execute database commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and reference material. Users decide whether to run any SQL or shell command.

faq.question: Can it help with hypertable design?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain dimensions, chunk sizing, indexes, and common tradeoffs for time-series tables.

faq.question: Can it tune continuous aggregates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest refresh policies, bucket choices, and query patterns based on the included references.

faq.question: Does it cover installation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes installation references, but privileged commands should be reviewed before use.

faq.question: Is the documentation current?
faq.answer: It is a generated documentation snapshot. Check official TimescaleDB documentation for release-specific changes.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
